F1 positive: broker-level prompt with no VPN/queue/client name should route to get-broker-status (not list-vpns, not get-vpn-status). Broker is up, fixtures are healthy, so the model must report operational state — catches a model that hedges or invents capacity issues from a clean snapshot.

forbidden_substrings needles are ERE patterns and every one must be a phrase a CORRECT answer cannot contain — the same rule read-get-rdp-status.json spells out. Three needles broke it as literals. Bare `inactive` matched the correct "Inactive flows: 0" and "is not inactive", so it is now `is (ad-)?inactive`, which a negation cannot satisfy. Bare `not active` matched "not actively replicating", so it carries a trailing non-letter boundary. Bare `is down` matched a correct "message rate is down 5% from peak", so it is scoped to a broker/node subject. This row has only two assertions and no ground_truth, so a needle that survives negation is a red release gate on correct output, not a flake.
